Which length is the greatest?
A pediatric dose is 0.25 mg. How many micrograms (mcg) is this?
Which statement best describes a scientific theory?
options: An educated guess that has not yet been tested
A law that has not yet been proven
The result of a single experiment
A well-tested explanation backed by evidence

stem: A company claims its new hand sanitizer reduces infections in hospital units. Which finding would most weaken this claim?
options: Infection rates were the same with or without it.
Some nurses said the sanitizer had an unpleasant smell.
The sanitizer costs more than plain soap.
Nurses who used the sanitizer said they liked it.

stem: Which is an example of deductive reasoning?
options: Several patients improved on a drug, so it will work for every patient.
Every swan I have seen is white, so all swans are white.
All mammals have hair; a dolphin is a mammal; so a dolphin has hair.
The sun has risen every day so far, so it will rise tomorrow.

stem: A survey finds that people who drink more coffee report more headaches. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Coffee causes headaches in most people.
Headaches cause people to drink more coffee.
The survey proves there is no link.
They are linked, but the survey can't show cause.

stem: A student wants evidence that music makes plants grow taller. Which steps would make the evidence stronger? Select all that apply.
options: Use many plants in each group.
Randomly assign plants to the music and no-music groups.
Play music only to the plants that already look healthiest.
Keep light, water and soil the same for both groups.
Ask a friend whether the music plants look taller.

stem: In a lab, a student adds drops of an indicator to a clear solution. Which statement is an observation?
options: A new compound must have formed.

stem: A study of 20 volunteers found that Supplement Z improved memory. Which would make this result most trustworthy?
options: The study was paid for by the company that sells Z.
The volunteers were told they were taking Z.
The result was widely shared on social media.
Independent teams repeated it with more people.

stem:
The table shows how much sugar dissolves in 100 mL of water at different temperatures:

Temperature | Sugar dissolved
20 °C | 204 g
40 °C | 238 g
60 °C | 287 g
80 °C | 362 g

Based on the pattern, how much sugar would most likely dissolve at 100 °C?
In a forest, foxes eat rabbits. After a mild winter, the fox population grows sharply and the rabbit population falls. What is most likely to happen next to the fox population?
options: It will decrease as food becomes scarce.
It will keep growing at the same rate.
It will stay exactly the same.
It will grow faster because there are fewer rabbits.

stem: A gas in a sealed container occupies 6 L at a pressure of 2 atm. If the temperature stays the same and the pressure is raised to 4 atm, what will the volume be?

Speed | Heart rate
0 mph | 70 bpm
3 mph | 95 bpm
5 mph | 130 bpm
7 mph | 165 bpm

What is the best prediction of heart rate at 6 mph?
Air pressure decreases as altitude increases. A sealed bag of chips is packed at sea level and carried up a mountain. What will most likely happen to the bag?
options: It will stay the same size.
It will lose air through the seal.

stem: A person becomes dehydrated. Put these events in the order they occur.
A bacterial population doubles every 30 minutes. If it starts with 500 bacteria, how many will there be after 2 hours?
A nurse tests whether a new type of dressing makes wounds heal faster than the standard dressing. What is the dependent variable?
options: The time it takes wounds to heal
The number of nurses on the unit

stem: In a drug study, Group 1 receives the new drug and stays in private rooms. Group 2 receives a placebo and stays in a shared ward. What is the main flaw in this design?
options: The placebo group should also get the drug.
The sample size is too large.
The groups differ in more than one way.

stem: A student tests how the amount of sunlight affects plant growth. Which is a controlled variable?
options: The number of leaves that grow

stem: A scientist's results do not support her hypothesis. What should she do?
options: Report the results and test a revised hypothesis.
Adjust the data so it matches the hypothesis.
Throw out the results and report nothing.
Repeat only the trials that agreed with the hypothesis.

stem: Why do scientists repeat trials in an experiment?
options: To make the data look more impressive
To reduce the effect of chance errors
To change the hypothesis partway through
To avoid needing a separate control group

stem: Which are characteristics of a good scientific hypothesis? Select all that apply.
options: It could be shown to be wrong.
It is based on personal opinion.
It has already been proven true.
